overall:
The reading question decides the result.

**Which readings are consistent.** Two readings of U = −G̃m²W(|v−v′|/v*)/|x−x′| are consistent dynamics:
- (i) a Hamiltonian with the gate on canonical momenta, which gives an anomalous velocity ẋ = p/m + ∂U/∂p;
- (ii) a Lagrangian with the gate on velocities.

They coincide at O(ε). The agent's force law (iii) is a well-posed, reversible, momentum-conserving ODE, but no Hamiltonian H = T + U or Lagrangian L = T − U produces it: T + U is not conserved and phase-space volume is not preserved.

**Which reading the record uses.** It is (i). Lab notebook §5.2 writes 'ẋ ⊃ ∇ₚε — an anomalous velocity'; calc note #2 writes ε(x,p); #11 §8 gates the amplitude on the incoming relative momentum. In calc note #2's static homogeneous medium the anomalous velocity drops out; about the Hubble flow it does not.

**The agent's linear system matches none of them.** It is a hybrid. Its density kernel R(y) = y∫sin(yt)W dt is wrong for its own stated force law: brute force gives R₁ = ∫₀¹R(yμ)dμ, 2.58 times smaller at the pivot. It then adds the force-law anti-drag, which is correct. My implementation of the agent's system reproduces K5, K6 and K8 exactly, so the error is in the model, not the arithmetic.
